decision: Does transplanting openLBMPM's compressed fluid-node neighbour table (CSR-like fluid-node compaction + flat 8-entry neighbour array with a -1 solid sentinel and in-place half-way bounce-back, periodic wrap at table build time) into TensorLBM reproduce the reference physics (Darcy permeability k, mean velocity, field-shape) within the owner 15% criterion, and what does the representation buy in memory footprint and iteration speed at fixed porosity?

alternatives.A1_compressed_oss_transplant: TensorLBM porous.FluidNodeTable: K=#fluid compaction, flat neighbour array (K,8) with -1 sentinel, push streaming with in-place half-way bounce-back, periodic wrap baked in at build time (OSS semantics)
alternatives.A2_dense_inrepo_control: TensorLBM full-lattice pull streaming (tensorlbm.d2q9.stream, torch.roll) + solid-mask half-way bounce-back at fluid nodes whose destination neighbour is solid; identical collision, identical Guo forcing, identical geometry
alternatives.A3_analytic: Poiseuille permeability k = H^2/12 for a plane channel of lattice width H driven by constant body force g (half-way bounce-back places the wall at 0.5 dx)

hypothesis: H1: the compressed representation is physics-neutral: every KPI of A1 equals A2 to representation round-off (relative deviation < 1e-8), and A1/A2 reproduce A3 within the owner 15% band. H0 (falsifier): any KPI deviates >= 1e-8 relative between A1 and A2 (representation bug: wrap, sentinel, stencil order or bounce-back mismatch), or >= 15% between A1 and A3.

metrics.k_darcy: Darcy permeability k = nu * <u_x>_superficial / g, lattice units; <u_x>_superficial = sum(u_x over fluid nodes)/N_total
metrics.ux_field_maxabs_rel: max|u_x(A1)-u_x(A2)| / max|u_x(A2)| on fluid nodes, per steady-state snapshot
metrics.mass_drift: |sum(rho) - sum(rho_0)| / sum(rho_0) over the run (mass conservation of the push scheme)
metrics.table_bytes: bytes held by the compressed state (9*K float64 PDF + (K,8) int64 table + K int64 map) vs the dense state (9*N float64 PDF + N bool mask)
metrics.mlups: N_total * steps / elapsed_seconds / 1e6, wall clock, single CPU process, float64
metrics.k_porosity_curve: k(porosity) at porosity = 0.60, 0.75, 0.90 (square grains, body force along x) -- sensitivity arm, compared against the Carman-Kozeny band as an informational reference, NOT an acceptance metric

unit_of_analysis: one completed simulation arm at fixed (geometry, resolution, tau, g, steps); KPIs are scalars (or fields for the difference metrics)

baseline_control.physical_baseline: A3 analytic Poiseuille k = H^2/12 (plane channel, H = number of fluid rows)
baseline_control.representation_control: A2 dense full-lattice implementation sharing collision, forcing, geometry and steady-state criterion with A1 -- the only changed variable is the data layout / streaming scheme
baseline_control.oss_note: the OSS code is CUDA (numba.cuda) and needs a GPU + its own Shan-Chen multiphase setup; this environment has no GPU, so the OSS arm is a semantics-exact transplant of its neighbour-table build and streaming rules into TensorLBM (cited line by line), not an execution of the OSS binary. This is recorded as a comparison limit, not silently upgraded.

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: H1 holds iff every KPI of A1 vs A2 is < 1e-8 relative AND every physical KPI of A1 vs A3 is < 15%; the representation-identity threshold is deliberately 9 orders stricter than the owner band because a representation change must be exact, and only the physics-vs-analytic comparison uses the 15% band
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: a KPI is resolution-converged when |KPI(N=256)-KPI(N=128)|/|KPI(N=256)| < 5%; otherwise the finer value is reported and the resolution delta is reported as a sensitivity result
predeclared_thresholds.linearity_rule: k must be independent of the body force: |k(g=2e-4)-k(g=1e-4)|/|k(g=1e-4)| < 5% (Darcy regime check, Ma = g*H^2/(8*nu*cs) must stay < 0.1)
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a run producing a non-finite population, rho outside [0.95, 1.05], or Ma > 0.1 is declared failed and reported, never tuned away

stopping_rule: every arm runs a step count fixed before the run (see run_config.steps in the runner) and stops early only when the predeclared steady-state criterion max|u(n)-u(n-200)|/max|u(n)| < 1e-9 is met; no arm is extended after looking at KPIs. Wall-clock budget 900 s per arm; anything above that is moved to the cluster queue.
variables_changed: data representation (compressed fluid-node table / dense full lattice)
porosity (1.00 plane channel, 0.90, 0.75, 0.60 square-grain porous medium)
body force g (1e-4, 2e-4) at fixed porosity 0.75
variables_held_fixed: Guo body-force forcing (velocity shift + force term), identical formula in both arms
half-way bounce-back on solid, periodic wrap in both directions
float64 throughout, single CPU thread, torch 2.7.1
confounders: memory access order differs between push(compressed) and pull(dense) -- affects wall time, not the converged field
the dense arm integrates the same physics on wasted solid nodes, so its cost is an upper bound for the representation benefit, not a hardware-independent constant
half-way bounce-back wall location (0.5 dx outside the last fluid node) must be accounted for in the analytic channel width H, otherwise a ~3% geometric bias appears at H=32
int64 neighbour table in the transplant (OSS also uses int64) overstates the table memory; an int32 variant is reported as the practical footprint
analysis: grouped by arm; no outlier removal; errors are relative to the analytic value or to the A2 control; uncertainty is the spread between the two resolutions; convergence and forcing-linearity are reported as separate sensitivity tables
fail_stage_plan: if the transplant fails, fail_stage names the stage (table_build / streaming / bounce_back / forcing / analysis) and the failure_reason carries the measured deviation

amendments.what: metric definition clarified: 'k_darcy' in 'metrics' is the SUPERFICIAL (Darcy) permeability nu*<u>_all_sites/g; the analytic anchor 'k = H^2/12' is an INTRINSIC (fluid-average) permeability, so the channel reference is k_ref = porosity * H^2/12 = (H/ny)*H^2/12.
amendments.why: first channel run gave k_super = 8.524 versus the raw H^2/12 = 21.33 (ratio 0.402 = the slab porosity H/ny = 16/40); the converged velocity profile was already parabolic to 0.2% (u_max 3.181e-3 vs 3.1875e-3 analytic), so this is a definition mismatch, not a solver deviation. Both the intrinsic and the superficial numbers are reported from now on; no KPI was redefined after inspecting a favourable result, and the raw numbers are kept.
